label: late original-phase input of a first-occurrence token from {o,m,x,k,d,f,e,r,p,3,w,z} when the sequence did not start with one
explanation: 95% of the activation mass falls in the original (input) phase, at positions t>=3, peaking at t=4-7. It never fires at t=0-1 and is close to silent in the copy phase. A smaller share (about 5%) comes from the <DEL> step. The current input token matters most: o, m, x and k have the highest rate (3-4x lift), then d, f, e, r, p, 3, w and z. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of that token (in_first=1 carries 88% of the mass). It is stronger when the sequence started with y, i, g, 0 or l (the first-token lift is about 3x for y). It is weaker when o/m/x/k already appeared earlier, including as the first token. The largest activations are o/m/x inputs at t=4-6 in sequences beginning y y ... The pattern looks like a graded mix of current-token and earlier-token effects, not a clean rule. The simpler predicate (orig phase, t>=3, in_tok in the 12-token set) has mass recall 0.83 but precision 0.35. It does not fire on y/i/g/0/l/a/b/j as inputs or during copy output.
